title: Limit Toast Queue
prompt: A React toast system should keep only the newest notifications on screen. Write a helper that appends the next toast and returns only the last maxToasts items.

explanation.beginner:
Example: limitToastQueue([{"id":"1","message":"One"}], {"id":"2","message":"Two"}, 3) produces [{"id":"1","message":"One"},{"id":"2","message":"Two"}]. The result must follow this precise rule: A React toast system should keep only the newest notifications on screen. Write a helper that appends the next toast and returns only the last maxToasts items. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “drops oldest over the limit”: input [[{"id":"1","message":"One"},{"id":"2","message":"Two"}],{"id":"3","message":"Three"},2] produces [{"id":"2","message":"Two"},{"id":"3","message":"Three"}]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
